hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Two, in order. Zero builds first: `fnasm game/mb/mb_camera.c MBWorldToScreen3D --ours` and count the distinct FPRs; ours is 13 today. Then one build: `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/mb/mb_camera.c MBWorldToScreen3D --ops --no-slots`. If the distinct-FPR count is still 13 and the multiset is still exactly `target-only: +1 lfd +1 stfd`, then naming the x-half operands does not raise peak pressure either, and the whole pressure account should be abandoned in favour of treating this as MWCC scheduler policy and parking the function on the source axis for good.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-ASYMMETRIC by construction and unavoidably so: the cure must ADD two instructions (the stfd/lfd pair) and 8 bytes of frame, taking ours from 102 to 104 and 128 to 136. Naming operands that are already loaded is itself count-NEUTRAL -- the loads and the fmuls already exist in both streams -- so any form that CHANGES the count in either direction has hit a different mechanism and is not a test of this hypothesis. That is also why no postprocessor class can ever serve this function.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- every offset, register and instruction quoted above is read from this run's own `fnasm --diff` and `--ours` dumps at 0f4151839 and is accurate, and the 1:1 instruction correspondence is the predecessor's census reproduced. What is NOT screened is whether the target's source actually names the x-half operands: no evidence beyond the symmetry argument and the register count supports it, and the mapping of f31's value `212(r10)` to `camera->viewport[1][1]` is inferred from `@0x150 fmuls f0,f12,f31` matching the source's `yDenomA * yDenomB` product with `@0x140 lfs f12,148(r10)` as `camera->projection[1][1]`, not from an independent layout check.
hypothesis.statement: The residual is a peak-FP-PRESSURE difference and the carrier is the X HALF's missing named locals, not the y half's yoff read. Measured this run: the target uses fifteen distinct FPRs (f0-f13 plus the callee-saved f31 at `@0x13c lfs f31,212(r10)`, consumed at `@0x150 fmuls f0,f12,f31`) where ours uses thirteen, and the instruction streams correspond 1:1 apart from the save pair, so the extra registers come from LIVE RANGES, not from extra values. MWCC prices live ranges on the pre-schedule IR, i.e. in SOURCE ORDER -- which is why f31 holds a value whose SCHEDULED range is only 0x14 long. In our source the Y half names its three operands (`yDenomB = camera->viewport[1][1]; yDenomA = camera->projection[1][1]; yDepthScale = camera->viewport[3][1];` at lines 107-109, live to line 120) while the X HALF names none of its three -- `camera->viewport[3][0]`, `camera->projection[0][0]` and `camera->viewport[0][0]` are written inline at lines 113-115. That asymmetry is not something a programmer writing these two halves would produce, and it is exactly worth the missing pressure: naming the x-half's three operands beside the y-half's three gives three more IR live ranges spanning the f64 block and the x-half division. Probe the SYMMETRIC form -- add `xDenomB`, `xDenomA`, `xDepthScale` assigned immediately before or beside lines 107-109 and use them at lines 113-115 -- and read the result on the multiset delta and on the distinct-FPR count, never on real.
